task_brief: Visual art concept work on paint or color media. Visual art concept: mix, place, or compare colour and value relationships through paint or color media, then use observable evidence to explain or revise a learner-owned decision. Complete the independent work yourself and explain the reason for each main choice.
primary_task: Target for this model_a session: Build a clear mental model of paint or color media through an explicit worked example, demonstration, text, or phenomenon. Use subject-appropriate evidence or representation to communicate understanding of paint or color media. Check, revise, or improve work about paint or color media using stated success criteria. Closing evidence check: In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about paint or color media; then identify one check that would catch an error or weak claim. What paint or color media means here: Colour names a hue; value names how light or dark it is. Mood comes from relationships among choices, not from one universal colour meaning. How the relationship changes the result: Changing value contrast changes visibility and emphasis; changing saturation or temperature changes energy and distance when viewed beside another colour. Choice and tradeoff: Strong contrast can improve clarity but reduce subtle transitions. Closely related values can feel unified but may need pattern or labels for access. Worked example: Two blue shapes can separate clearly when one is pale and one is dark; two different hues can disappear together when their values match. Non-example: Calling every red energetic or every blue calm ignores context, culture, value, saturation, and the maker’s intent. 1. Guided practice: Complete the first supported pass on paint or color media with the supplied model or scaffold visible. Make two short studies, keep one relationship stable, change one hue, and circle the exact cue you will remove next time. 2. Independent creation: Create a fresh, bounded work involving paint or color media. State an intent, choose at least two relevant relationships, preserve one intermediate state, check the result, and make or deliberately decline one revision with a reason. 3. Reflection: Compare an earlier and later state. Name the choice that changed, cite what became visible, audible, notated, or workable, and state the next revision or reason to keep the result. 4. Critique: Describe before judging. Locate evidence, compare it with the maker’s stated intent, ask one genuine question, and offer options; the maker keeps final authority. A private self-critique receives full credit. 5. Knowledge check: Explain how one choice changes the effect in paint or color media, distinguish the worked example from the non-example, and describe the tradeoff in your own words. Your choices remain yours: Different palette, medium, mood or purpose, contrast strategy, revision after the access check choices are valid when the learner meets objective constraints and supports the result with evidence. Use the attached Manuel Academy resource in this package. It gives you the model, example, or help sheet needed for this task. Keep today's work tied to your unit. Today is about paint or color media. It is part of "Materials, Techniques, and Design". Later days in this unit cover other things, like drawing tools. Before you stop, do this check: In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about paint or color media; then identify one check that would catch an error or weak claim. In grade 5, finish on your own. Write a reason for each main choice. If there were two ways to do it, say which one you picked and why.

ATTACHED MANUEL ACADEMY LEARNER RESOURCE

Resource ID: ma-resource:ma-g5-arts-and-music-u02-l02

Lesson focus: paint or color media

Resource type: ACADEMY_ORIGINAL_MODEL

MODEL A — “One relationship at a time.” Colour names a hue; value names how light or dark it is. Mood comes from relationships among choices, not from one universal colour meaning. Changing value contrast changes visibility and emphasis; changing saturation or temperature changes energy and distance when viewed beside another colour. Worked example for paint or color media: Two blue shapes can separate clearly when one is pale and one is dark; two different hues can disappear together when their values match. Starting state: state the intended effect, question, or criterion before acting. First decision: locate hue, value, saturation, temperature, adjacency, pattern, and labelled contrast. Intermediate state: complete one bounded study, loop, map, or comparison while most features stay stable. Check: cite what changed before judging it. Finished or intentionally partial result: keep the evidence even when it challenges the first intention. Common misapplication: Calling every red energetic or every blue calm ignores context, culture, value, saturation, and the maker’s intent. Legitimate variation: another learner may choose different palette, medium, mood or purpose, contrast strategy, revision after the access check and still meet the criterion. Use it to study paint or color media; describe evidence before judging and adapt the demonstrated relationship rather than copying a finished work.

How to use it: Use the attached Manuel Academy resource in this package. It gives you the model, example, or help sheet needed for this task.

Rights: Manuel Academy original; licensed CC BY 4.0 for learner use and adaptation. No third-party text, image, score, lyric, melody, recording, or performance is included.

presentation_and_privacy.presentation_options: You choose the audience. Keeping the work entirely to yourself, showing it to one parent or trusted adult, or submitting it as a file with no one watching are all full-credit options. No public performance, exhibition, class presentation, live audience, photograph, camera, or voice recording is required at any point in this task, and choosing the most private option never lowers the score.
presentation_and_privacy.text_or_no_audio_alternative: A written alternative is always available for spoken reflection, explanation, or critique and scores the same. Use a labelled visual, tactile, constructed, or accessible digital work to preserve the making target; prose alone does not claim visual or material technique evidence. You may describe the work in writing and have one trusted adult verify a physical artifact without photographing you or your home. No microphone, camera, or recording is required.

copyright_and_authorship: The graded submission must be your own authorship. A parent, tutor, or AI tool may explain an idea, demonstrate a technique, or give feedback on a draft, but must not produce, write, debug, or make any part of the work that is scored. Any material you did not create yourself must be in the public domain, openly licensed, or used as a short cited excerpt for study — reproduce no more than the point requires, credit the maker and the source, and never copy full lyrics, a complete score, or a whole image and present it as your own.
accessibility_options: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, manipulatives-based, or demonstrated responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
task_accessibility_provisions: This task uses things you look at (paint or color media). You may use raised or textured materials, very large print, strong colours, or a spoken description instead.
You may use low-smell, low-dust materials, and you can sit or stand to work. Ask for chunkier handles or grips if that helps.
Anything you have to study will also come as plain text, a described version, or a version you can touch.
You can take a break, stretch, or come back to this later. That does not lower your score.
safety_and_privacy_rules: Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Protect hearing, ventilation, tool safety, copyright, cultural context, and respectful representation.
Provide a non-performance or low-audience option when needed without lowering the academic target.

media.fallback: Use the complete adjacent verbal description and recreate the relationships with raised or movable paper forms. The required Academy model is attached; no outside search is needed.

remediation: Route 1: Reduce paint or color media to three locatable events, areas, steps, or decisions. Label the intended effect beside each and underline the one hue relationship that should carry it. Use a separate small study, four-event loop, thumbnail, evidence table, or paper plan. The adult may model the noticing process on different material but may not change the learner’s work. Check yourself: Point to or name the exact hue evidence before deciding whether it serves the intent. New attempt: Put the support away and make a new arrangement, passage, response, or plan; record what the new evidence shows. Route 2: Return to the last understandable state. Hold every relationship steady except one chosen feature from hue, value, saturation, temperature, adjacency, pattern, and labelled contrast; predict what that single change should do. Test the feature on scrap paper, a silent count, a two-event rehearsal loop, movable shapes, or a short evidence sentence before changing the scored work. Check yourself: Name what stayed the same, what changed, and the first observable result—without using “better” as the evidence. New attempt: Create a different small case using the same one-variable method, then transfer the finding to the original task only if it serves the learner’s intent.
extension: Apply paint or color media under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or teach the idea with an original example without completing another learner’s graded work. Treat this as optional depth on paint or color media rather than extra volume: one harder case done well beats three more of the same. Extension work stays private by default and uses only original, public-domain, or properly cited material. Extension work is never required to reach mastery and must not be assigned as a penalty.
